sourceFacts.fact: Untreated or poorly transfused severe beta-thalassaemia can cause marked anaemia and expansion of erythroid marrow.
Expansion of marrow can produce skeletal and craniofacial changes, including frontal bossing.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Thalassaemia: demand expands the marrow'. Four simple objects on a left-to-right causal conveyor. FIRST a low fill-level gauge labelled 'Severe anaemia'. SECOND a small factory control lever pushed upward, labelled 'More production drive'. THIRD a flat warehouse icon growing from a small outlined footprint to a larger teal footprint, labelled 'Marrow expansion'. FOURTH a simple firm rectangular frame being pushed outward by two abstract outward arrows, label 'Bone shape can change'. These are industrial demand/capacity metaphors; no red cells, bone cross-section, skull, tissue, organs or patient faces. Bottom qualifying text 'Untreated or poorly transfused disease'. Clear one-way arrows between stages; no claim all anaemia or all treated thalassaemia causes these changes.
